questions.question: What is an array?
options: A collection of similar data types
questions.explanation: An array is a collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations.

questions.question: Array indices typically start from:
questions.explanation: In most programming languages, array indexing starts from 0.

questions.question: How many elements can be stored in an array declared as `arr[10]`?
questions.explanation: An array declared with size 10 can store exactly 10 elements (indices 0 to 9).

questions.question: Which operation adds an element to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: Push adds an element to the end of an array.

questions.question: What does the Pop operation do?
questions.explanation: Pop removes and returns the last element from an array.

questions.question: To insert an element at position 2 in an array, which elements need to be shifted?
questions.explanation: Elements from position 2 onwards must shift right to make space for the new element.

questions.question: What is linear search?
options: Checking each element one by one
questions.explanation: Linear search checks each element sequentially until the target is found or the array ends.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search?
questions.explanation: In the worst case, linear search must check every element, making it O(n).

questions.question: Binary search requires the array to be:
questions.explanation: Binary search works only on sorted arrays because it divides the search space based on comparison.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm works by repeatedly swapping adjacent elements if they are in wrong order?
questions.explanation: Bubble Sort repeatedly steps through the list, compares adjacent elements, and swaps them if needed.

questions.question: In Selection Sort, the array is divided into:
questions.explanation: Selection Sort maintains a sorted portion at the beginning and an unsorted portion at the end.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm has the best average-case time complexity?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort has O(n log n) average and worst case, which is better than the O(n²) of Bubble, Selection, and Insertion Sort.

questions.question: How does a list differ from an array?
options: Lists can grow and shrink dynamically
questions.explanation: Lists can dynamically grow and shrink in size, unlike arrays which have a fixed size.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of inserting at the beginning of an array?
questions.explanation: Inserting at the beginning requires shifting all existing elements, making it O(n).

questions.question: A 2D array is best visualized as:
options: A table with rows and columns
questions.explanation: A 2D array has rows and columns, like a table or matrix.

questions.question: How do you access the element in row 2, column 3 of a 2D array `arr`?
questions.explanation: In most languages, 2D array elements are accessed using row index first, then column index: arr[row][col].

questions.question: Aisha has an array [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]. She wants to insert 25 at position 2. What will the array look like?
questions.explanation: Inserting 25 at position 2 shifts elements from position 2 onwards: [10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50].

questions.question: A teacher has a sorted list of 1000 student roll numbers. Which search method is most efficient?
questions.explanation: For a sorted list of 1000 elements, binary search takes at most 10 comparisons (log₂1000 ≈ 10), while linear search may need 1000.

questions.question: Which data structure uses LIFO (Last In, First Out)?
questions.explanation: A stack follows LIFO — the last element pushed is the first one popped.

questions.question: Hassan is sorting exam marks [85, 72, 93, 65, 88] in ascending order using Bubble Sort. After the first pass, what will the array look like?
questions.explanation: After first pass of Bubble Sort: [72, 85, 65, 88, 93]. The largest element (93) bubbles to the end.
